dimensions.assessment: Affects airmen, air traffic control specialists, individuals training in aviation, medical examiners, and doctors.
dimensions.evidence: aviation stakeholders, including airmen, air traffic control specialists, and individuals training to become airmen or air traffic control specialists

dimensions.assessment: Provides transparency and guidance on permitted medications without changing underlying safety standards or assuming liability.
dimensions.evidence: The publication of the list described in subsection (b) shall not be construed as assigning liability to the Administrator

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not state specific federal spending or economic costs associated with creating and maintaining the list.
Requires the FAA to establish and maintain a new publicly accessible website list and consult with multiple aviation and medical organizations.
dimensions.evidence: publish and maintain on a publicly available website of the Federal Aviation Administration a list of medications

dimensions.assessment: Establishes an ongoing requirement to maintain and annually update the medication list on a permanent basis.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 1 year after the date of publication of the list required under subsection (b)... the Administrator shall update such list

missing_information: Specific federal funding allocations or costs for implementing the website and list.
Exact number of pilots, air traffic controllers, or medical professionals who will use the list.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill directs the FAA to compile, publish, and annually update a public list of approved and prohibited medications for pilots and air traffic controllers, affecting aviation stakeholders, medical providers, and applicants for medical certification.
